spans.reaching_argument: `path`, a parameter of protected method read_lines(path, selector). The fix only renamed it from `filename`.
spans.receiver_dispatch: Constant receiver IO, class method foreach. A String argument beginning with "|" spawns a subprocess (Ruby < 4.0; deprecated in 3.3). The receiver resolves statically; this is not dynamic dispatch.
spans.fixed_revision_guard: Same-file caller: process() passes path = resolve_target_path(target, reader). At the fixed revision that returns target only when target_http?(target) (downcased http:// or https:// prefix and URI.parse is URI::HTTP), otherwise reader.document.normalize_system_path(target, reader.dir, ...) kept only if ::File.file?(path). Neither value can begin with '|'. The guard is interprocedural (process -> resolve_target_path -> read_lines), outside a local matcher.
spans.note: The old side has the same call (renamed argument), so any local matcher hits both sides equally. The fix is in target_http?/resolve_target_path.
spans.label: NOT_ADJUDICATED

spans.receiver_dispatch: Constant receiver URI (open-uri). For a String that is not an http/https/ftp URI, URI.open falls back to Kernel#open, where "|cmd" runs a command. The receiver resolves statically.

Neither value can begin with '|'. The guard is interprocedural (process -> resolve_target_path -> read_lines), outside a local matcher.

reasons: In both cases the fix is upstream of the sink. GHSA-6g56 adds cross-file API validation, and its quoting alone is insufficient. GHSA-v222 narrows the same-file caller with target_http? and path normalization. The sink lines are identical or renamed on both sides.
Any parameter-to-sink matcher that hits the old-side hunk therefore also emits the same fixed-side spans (5 Go, 2 Ruby). Treating the Go single quotes as a sanitizer would be unprincipled.

Fixed-side check on the current exposed pair (baseline 8cd65488 -> candidate b2a2800f, OpenGrep 2.1.0): residuals 17/39 hits -> 18/40. The unchanged limit allows a per-hit rate of at most 17/39 x 1.1 = 0.4795. Recovering both cases (+2 hits) with all 7 spans gives 25/42 = 0.595. Dropping the 2 receiver-result spans still gives 23/42 = 0.548. No replacement within the existing names and thresholds passes the fixed-side check.
The two s.vgName(vgid) spans come from tainting receiver-method results. A replacement must drop that, whatever the cohort shows.
